title: Nested Routes
description: Learn how to create nested route structures for complex layouts.

data.text: **Nested routes** allow you to create hierarchical URL structures and render components inside other components. This is useful for shared layouts.

data.title: Nested Routes
data.code:
<Routes>
  <Route path="/" element={<Layout />}>
    <Route index element={<Home />} />
    <Route path="about" element={<About />} />
    <Route path="dashboard" element={<Dashboard />}>
      <Route index element={<DashboardHome />} />
      <Route path="stats" element={<Stats />} />
      <Route path="settings" element={<Settings />} />
    </Route>
  </Route>
</Routes>

data.text: The **Outlet** component renders the child route's element. It's placed inside the parent layout component.

data.title: Outlet

data.text: An **index route** renders when the parent route's path matches exactly. It's the default child route.

data.title: Layout Routes
data.text: Use layout routes (routes without a path) to wrap multiple routes with shared UI without adding to the URL.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Nested routes create hierarchical URL structures
Index routes render at parent's exact path
Layout routes wrap routes with shared UI
data.takeaway: Nested routes enable complex, organized layouts.
